title: The Essential Corridor
briefing: Emergency purchasing and disrupted deliveries have left warehouses unevenly stocked. Clinics need filters, repair crews need components, and shops need food. A limited freight corridor can reopen, but fuel, loading crews and bridge capacity cannot serve every destination today.

private_intelligence.infrastructure: The old river bridge needs a restricted-load repair window. A priority corridor can combine deliveries with that work; unrestricted commercial routing would postpone inspection and increase fatigue damage.
private_intelligence.community: Outer neighbourhoods have fewer shops and cannot bid against large buyers. A corridor serving only institutions may still be seen as abandonment unless residents can see when household deliveries will resume.
private_intelligence.economy: Emergency bulk purchase would consume $4.2M above the normal budget. Auctioning freight slots raises cash quickly, but essential suppliers say they cannot match supermarket bids.
private_intelligence.safety: Municipal takeover can place clinical supplies first today. Corridor scheduling is safer for crews but leaves several small clinics dependent on a one-day buffer whose inventory figures are uncertain.

choices.title: Purchase and Commandeer
choices.description: Buy the available stock at emergency prices and redirect depot crews to urgent city orders.
choices.consequence: Urgent supplies reach care teams and reduce immediate harm. Costly purchases drain reserves, compulsory redirection damages legitimacy, and rushed freight movements wear the network.

choices.title: Auction Freight Access
choices.description: Sell scarce freight slots and let suppliers choose destinations through the existing market.
choices.consequence: Slot revenue and resumed trade improve finances. Uninspected routes deteriorate, poorer districts lose out, and uneven access increases both safety risks and public resentment.

choices.title: Build a Priority Corridor
choices.description: Reserve a restricted route for essential freight, bridge repairs and a published household delivery schedule.
choices.consequence: Coordinated repairs strengthen the route and visible scheduling restores confidence. Reserved capacity reduces commercial revenue, while slower clinical deliveries leave immediate health risks.
